title: A Godot Plugin to Bridge the Gap (open source and available now)
author: josephsmithberger
selftext:
LLM's and agents haven't made as much of a dent into streamlining game dev as it has for other SWE fields. That's what I aimed to fix with this plugin! It has over 70 tools that leverage being Godot only, can run fully offline with local llm's (Gemma 4, Qwen 3.5...), is extremely context efficient, supports running the game and live debugging, and is open source! I am a game dev with a few games released w/o the use of ai. These are all tools that I thought would enhance my workflow.

**Please give it a star and try it out!!**

comments.author: HopefulMeasurement25
comments.body: How well does this compare against GodotIQ and their MCP plug-in? I need some honesty and some comparisons before I think about swapping over.

replies.author: josephsmithberger
replies.body: I haven't tried those out. I'll test them and let you know.

comments.author: Dan_Fury
comments.body:
I wish someone smarter than me could explain why we have half a dozen MCP solutions now instead of one big one where everyone cooperates. 

When I tested them all a month ago GoPeak by Had0Yun felt the best and Claude said he would prefer that one because of the working  run, inspect, modify and debug loop.

Is yours better? I see you have the same loop working. Will it not just cost more token because you don't deactivate the unnecessary tools and activate them on demand? That's something I saw others do.

Sorry if that sounds a bit harsh but I really just want to learn more about it.
I really wish someone could explain in detail about MCP because it's such a new technology and this is my first time using it. This sub needs a megathread about this topic that teaches about what is important and all the different things possible with it. Imho it's the most important thing in ai game dev.

E.g. I was really surprised when Claude told me it can animate my non humanoid character through MCP and I should let it try... it actually produced a usable animation when Mixamo and Autorig failed.

I bet there's a million use cases I haven't thought about.
